key_insight: UniClawBench introduces a universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive agents in realistic, tool-using, everyday scenarios. It aims to measure agent behavior more faithfully than sandboxed, single-turn benchmarks by reflecting the complexity of real-world tasks.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks for proactive AI agents are often too artificial, too limited to isolated turn-based interactions, and too mixed in what they measure. This makes it hard to fairly assess whether an agent can actually use tools, act proactively, and perform end-to-end tasks in real environments.
method: Defines a universal benchmark focused on real-world proactive agent tasks rather than synthetic sandbox settings.
Uses more realistic evaluation setups that better capture multi-step tool use and user-facing behavior.
Separates task categories more clearly so different capabilities are measured more cleanly and comparably.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more reliable way to test whether agents can function in practical settings beyond demos. It can improve model comparison, guide agent development, and reduce overfitting to narrow benchmark formats.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing proactive agent interaction with everyday tools and environment feedback.
A comparison chart contrasting sandbox benchmarks vs. UniClawBench on realism and evaluation quality.
An icon-based taxonomy of task types and capabilities being measured.
A scorecard/dashboard graphic summarizing multi-step task performance metrics.
paper_title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
paper_authors: Zhekai Chen, Chengqi Duan, Kaiyue Sun, Bohao Li, Yuqing Wang
